intro: People all over the world keep old stories. Grandparents tell them. Children learn them. Then the children tell them again.
In this unit you will hear stories from many groups. You will see special books and how people care for them. You will learn to say, "This is a story that ___ tell."
bigQuestion: Why do people keep stories and books safe for so long?

timeline.t: Grandpa tells Leo an old story
We hear the story of Noah and the ark
We hear about the prince who looked outside
We hear how lamps welcomed Rama home
We hear how Guru Nanak shared food
The librarian opens the glass case
We learn how people hold their holy books
We tell a story to a friend

words.d: a way a group of people believe, pray and live together
being kind and careful with what matters to someone else
the very big boat Noah builds in the story
a man who lives simply and spends his life on his religion
a Hindu festival of lights in the fall
a free meal Sikhs share with anyone who comes
a long sheet rolled up, not cut into pages
to say words out loud, often from memory

test.q: Who tells the story of Noah?
test.why: The Bible and Qur'an tell of Noah.

test.q: Who tells the story of Prince Siddhartha?
test.why: This is a story Buddhists tell.

test.q: What did Guru Nanak do with the money?
test.why: Sikhs call this the true trade.

test.q: Which holy book is a scroll?
test.why: The Torah rolls on two poles.
The Qur'an is the holy book of Islam.

test.q: Where do people keep holy books?
test.why: People keep them off the floor.

choices: To say words aloud from memory

test.q: What is a kind way to share a story?
choices: "This is a story that Hindus tell."
test.why: Naming who tells it is kind and true.

write.prompt: Pick one story or book from this unit. Draw it. Then say or write: "This is a story (or book) that ___ keep." Tell one way people care for it or one thing it helps them remember.
tips: Name the group: Jews, Christians, Muslims, Hindus, Buddhists or Sikhs.
Use one word from the unit, like scroll or langar.
Tell what people do, not what is best.
